chunks: God is not loath to advance the similitude of a gnat or a being more contemptible; and those who believe know whatever is from the Lord is true. But those who disbelieve say: "What does God mean by this parable?" He causes some to err this way, and some He guides; yet He turns away none but those who transgress,
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of the parable of the gnat in Surah Al-Baqarah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse (Ayat al-Mathal) highlights the divine wisdom in using both minute and grand examples to test the sincerity of believers versus the arrogance of disbelievers. It underscores that the 'misleading' of the Fasiqun (transgressors) is a consequence of their own pre-existing deviation, as God uses the parable to reveal their inner state. This concept is central to understanding how divine guidance and hiddenness operate simultaneously in the Quranic narrative.
